newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks open flat, focus on Van der Horst.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks open flat, focus on Van der Horst.

text.p: Singapore stocks were mostly flat at mid-morning on Thursday with focus still on engineering based Van der Horst, said dealers.

Van der Horst extended gains for the third consecutive day on speculative trading. Some dealers said there was renewed confidence in the company's longer term prospect despite its dismal first half earnings which plunged 84 percent.
The shares rose 22 cents to S$2.70 (US$1.89) on over 7.2 million units.
At 0215 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 2.09 at 2,021.77. Market turnover was moderate around 41 million shares with 88 gainers to 82 losers.
Focus continued to be on small issues. Sincere Watch rose S$0.05 to S$0.46 after its 1997 net profit jumped 154 percent to S$1.66 million.

Metal mould maker Lung Kee Metal Holding hit a new year high of US$1.18 before easing two cents to US$1.13 after better than expected 1997 earnings. Brokers said several reasearch houses maintained their buy recommendations on the stock.
DBS Bank continued to shine as some houses renewed a buy call on the stock on its growth prospects. The foreign tranche rose 10 cents to S$18.60 while the local units firmed five cents to S$8.65.
